Why Newark (EWR) Records Higher Delays


EWR experiences intersection constraints between parallel runway operations and high corporate hub banking from United Airlines. When convective weather halts Mid-Atlantic arrival gates, Newark ground hold durations escalate rapidly.






Why LaGuardia (LGA) Leads in Punctuality


LGA operates under federal perimeter slot controls that cap the total operations per hour, mitigating systemic over-scheduling and preserving high on-time reliability (81.1%).

title: Aviation Analytics
text:
1. Delay Accumulation Across the Operating Day
Each point below represents a commercial departure from New York City. Hover over any point to inspect its operating carrier, flight number, origin-destination city pair, and observed delay.








Figure 1








Morning Schedule Adherence


Flights departing between 05:00 and 08:30 AM tightly hug the zero baseline. Aircraft parked overnight are unencumbered by upstream network delays.






Afternoon Cascading Variance


After 14:00, departure delay variance widens substantially. Multi-leg aircraft utilization compounds small morning hiccups into severe late-day departures.







2. Departure Delay Distribution
Interactive histogram grouping 328,521 flights into 5-minute bins. Hover over any column to see exact departure counts. The red dashed line marks the FAA 15-minute threshold.








Figure 2








Modal Distribution


The single most frequent flight outcome is departing between 0 and 5 minutes ahead of schedule, proving baseline timetable viability.






Heavy Right Skew


Only 21.5% of flights cross the FAA 15-minute threshold, but severe delays form a persistent tail reaching several hours.







3. Carrier On-Time Performance Benchmark
Average departure delay in minutes across major airlines with at least 2,000 departures from New York metropolitan airports. Hover over any carrier bar to view complete operational figures:








Figure 3








Mainline Fleet Efficiency


US Airways (+3.8m), American (+8.6m), and Delta (+9.3m) demonstrate superior turnaround protocols and priority gate logistics.






Regional Carrier Exposure


ExpressJet (+20.0m) and AirTran (+18.7m) bear higher delay burdens due to multi-hop regional feeder structures and lower ATC priority.

Operational Summary
Across all 328,521 departed flights originating from New York City (JFK, LGA, EWR) in 2013, the majority left within standard operating windows:

  
    
      On-Time / Early
      60.9%
      200,089 flights (≤ 0 min)

      57,658 flights (1–15 min)

      8.1%
      26,581 flights (> 60 min)
    
  


60.9% departed early or on the exact scheduled minute.
17.6% experienced minor adjustments under 15 minutes, which commercial airlines classify as on-time under FAA standard A14 metrics.
21.5% incurred official delays exceeding 15 minutes.
8.1% suffered acute disruptions exceeding 60 minutes.




Official Delay Attribution (BTS Benchmark)
Official records from the Bureau of Transportation Statistics (BTS) and Federal Aviation Administration identify five core drivers of schedule delays:

  
    
      
        1. Late-Arriving Aircraft (Network Propagation)
        ~38%
      
      
      Planes fly multiple route segments each day. Upstream inbound delays automatically cascade downstream to subsequent flights.
    
  
  
    
      
        2. Air Carrier Operations
        ~30%
      
      
      Operational factors under carrier oversight: unscheduled maintenance, crew legal duty hour caps, ramp baggage handling, and cabin turnaround.
    
  
  
    
      
        3. NAS & Airspace Congestion
        ~24%
      
      
      Air traffic control route spacing, high terminal-area density, ground delay programs (GDP), and airport surface taxiway queues.
    
  
  
    
      
        4. Severe Weather Disruptions
        ~7%
      
      
      Meteorological events requiring airspace corridor rerouting or safety ground stops (thunderstorms, snowstorms, visibility minima).
    
  
  
    
      
        5. Security Breaches
        <1%
      
      
      Infrequent terminal concourse re-screenings or security perimeter hold procedures.
